A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MOCOBO. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization and reformatting.

before.justification: v3 reports original optimization experiments, peptide antibacterial assays, ablations, and runtime measurements in Section 4 and Appendix A.

after.justification: v4 retains those original empirical results and adds component and hyperparameter ablations in Appendix B.2.

M1.justification: The coverage objective, ECI acquisition, greedy covering-set construction, approximate batching, trust regions, and surrogate architecture remain unchanged. MOCOBO-EIT and MOCOBO without trust regions are added experimental controls, not revisions to the proposed algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions cover the same peptide, molecule, rover, and HDR tone-mapping tasks, including the highly conflicting three-course rover case. The new ablations reuse the existing four-course rover instance.

E2.justification: The main CluSO, TuRBO/LOL-BO, ROBOT, MORBO, random-sampling, and individually optimized solution comparisons remain. Figure B.9 adds two evaluated controls: MOCOBO without trust regions and MOCOBO-EIT, which replaces ECI with maximum per-objective expected improvement.

E3.justification: Appendix B.2 adds controlled rover sweeps over K=1,2,3,4; inducing-point counts 4,16,64,256,1024,4096; and batch sizes 1,2,5,10,20,40, plus component-removal controls. These extend experimental settings within the retained task and coverage-score evaluation.

E4.justification: v3's oracle-partition and conflicting-objective analyses are retained. v4 adds five substantive ablations examining covering-set size, surrogate quality, batch size, trust regions, and ECI. Figures B.6–B.9 substantially expand evidence about parameter sensitivity and the contributions of individual components.

E5.justification: Both versions specify 20 optimization replications with standard errors, 10 runtime repetitions with standard errors, and three biological replicates for antibacterial assays. The additional plots retain the existing uncertainty-reporting practice; no new statistical procedure or increased repeat count is stated.

E6.justification: Figures B.6–B.9 add substantial results: K=1 has poor coverage, larger covering sets converge faster, 4096 inducing points offer little benefit over 1024, batch sizes reach similar final coverage, and removing trust regions or replacing ECI reduces performance. These findings were absent from v3. The retained peptide MIC and runtime tables preserve their numerical values.

T1.justification: The coverage definitions, NP-hardness reduction, greedy approximation guarantee, complexity analysis, and acquisition mathematics are retained. Appendix I expands the explanation of the same binary encoding used in v3 Appendix A.9; it does not introduce a different reduction or substantive proof correction.

C1.justification: Both versions claim a BO approach to coverage optimization that handles structured, high-dimensional spaces, outperforms the evaluated alternatives, and finds small sets approaching individually optimized coverage. The antimicrobial claim remains coverage of nine pathogens with moderate activity against one additional pathogen. Rewritten contributions preserve these claims.

C2.justification: Appendix D adds substantive applicability discussion about generative-model pretraining requirements and threshold-based coverage. Section 4.2 newly attributes CluSO's weak performance to its mismatch with high-dimensional, structured tasks. Appendix B.2 adds explanations of surrogate accuracy versus computational cost and interpretations supporting the use of trust regions and ECI.

D1.justification: The new ablation sections document their hyperparameter grids and the construction of the EIT control. Existing surrogate, training, initialization, hardware, runtime, and code-access information is retained. Mentioning PPGPR in the main text repeats information already disclosed in v3's appendix.

R1.justification: v4 adds discussion distinguishing its ECI from Malkomes et al.'s coverage acquisition and Lee et al.'s extension, and expands latent-space and high-dimensional BO citations. The Gómez-Bombarelli et al. citation is removed. Positioning relative to Ding, Li, Lin, and CluSO is substantially retained.

P1.justification: The introduction and background are substantially rewritten, related work becomes a separate Section 5, and structured-search discussion moves into the experiments section. The appendix is reorganized into A–J with a contents listing, and the checklist moves before it. Terminology and proof explanations receive further editing.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is redrawn with reordered rover panels, revised ticks, and a reorganized legend. v3's combined Figures 3 and 4 become four larger, separate figures in v4. Four new ablation figures are added, while table captions, appendix placement, and the title block are extensively reformatted.

improvement.justification: v4 addresses an important validation gap: v3 evaluated complete optimizers and oracle partitioning, whereas Figure B.9 isolates ECI and trust-region contributions, and Figures B.6–B.8 test key parameter choices. Expanded applicability limitations and more legible figures further strengthen the paper's assessability. The new ablations concern only the four-course rover instance, but provide substantial additional support for the central design.
